text: This is Kaava. Ask a construction drawing a question, and see exactly where the answer came from.

How many doors are on this floor? The answer is not generated. It is counted from the drawing's own geometry: thirty-two door outlines, each one numbered on the plan and in the 3D model raised from it. A vision model alone said twenty-four.
The answer is marked Verified. That is a measured claim: on drawings held back for testing, answers of this kind were wrong eight times in more than six thousand.
Areas work the same way. Each room of the apartment fills with its square metres, and the balconies are left out, as the question asked.
Building models are queried directly, with no vision model involved. On this storey the query finds forty-two doors, each one marked on the plan and in the model, at no cost.
A scan has no geometry to query. Here Gemini draws a box around every window, and the code counts the boxes. Answers read from pixels are marked Check this, never Verified.
And this is why. On this plan it boxes twenty-three windows where the dataset says twenty. Every box is on the sheet, so a person can check each one, and leave out what does not belong.

On the same two hundred questions, a vision model alone is right sixty-two point five percent of the time. This system is right ninety-five point eight percent of the time, at forty percent of the cost. Sixty-nine answers were Verified. None of them was wrong.
Numbers computed, never generated. Evidence you can check in seconds. Kaava.
